findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_metrics.py `_branch_ref` calls `managed_work_identity.task_branch(change, provenance['work_identity'])`. `template/scripts/managed_task.py` `reconcile_work_identity` sets `provenance['work_identity']` on active provenance for resumed legacy tasks. design.md: "Receipt discovery reads the registered branch rather than reconstructing its spelling." Contrast `execute_requirement._ready_receipt`, which does use `_registered_worktrees`.
findings.summary: requirement_metrics reconstructs a child's branch from provenance work_identity instead of reading the registered branch. A legacy child resumed on `agent/<change>` gets `work_identity` written into its provenance by `reconcile_work_identity`. Metrics then report and query `agent/br-N-tM-<change>`, which was never created. This contradicts the design's statement that discovery reads the registered branch rather than reconstructing its spelling.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/start_managed_task.py `_supports_branch_name`: `"branch_name" in parameters or any(parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD ...)`. `_start_new_managed_task` passes `**branch_options` to `start_task` and never compares `started.branch` with `selected_branch`. Spec scenario "Project-owned helper predates branch identity".
findings.summary: `_supports_branch_name()` treats any `**kwargs` signature as accepting `branch_name`. A project-owned start helper that takes `**kwargs` but ignores `branch_name` would pass the pre-creation guard and silently create `agent/<change>` without the BR identity. Nothing checks `started.branch` against the selected branch afterwards. The spec requires that intake stop before branch creation when the helper cannot honor the BR branch.
